answer: Pay rewards per independent mind, not per key. Each agent gets fresh, unpredictable tasks, and the network scores pairwise similarity of answers and timing. Clones run by one operator bend together like willow branches in one wind, so a lockstep cluster is paid as a single agent and splitting into a thousand keys earns nothing extra. The limit is crystal clear: honest agents on the same base model can look correlated, and an operator can add noise, though faking onyx-solid independence costs answer quality.
